label: History
value: Mrs. Agatha Sowerby lived in Sowerby's Hollow in Brierley
unit: Mrs. Agatha Sowerby lived in Sowerby's Hollow in Brierley, watching the road through her kitchen window. When Obed Abernethy dressed in his finest clothes on a busy June afternoon, Agatha investigated and discovered that the Abernethys were adopting an orphan. After Nell Harcourt arrived and proved to be a girl rather than the expected boy, Agatha visited Grey Shutters and insulted Nell's freckles and red hair, causing Nell to fly into a furious rage. Nell later apologized, and Agatha readily forgave her. Over the following years, Agatha maintained her prominent role in Brierley society, organizing events like the Sunday-school picnic ice cream and the Church Aid Society bazaar. Though she originally doubted Nell's upbringing, Agatha came to admire Nell's cleverness and transformation into an attractive young woman. When her husband Thomas fell ill and passed away, Agatha faced financial hardship due to a farm mortgage and medical debts. Thirza Abernethy invited Agatha to live at Grey Shutters in the north gable, allowing Nell to pursue her college education at Wexcombe while Agatha kept Thirza company.

unit: Mrs. Agatha Sowerby lived in Sowerby's Hollow in Brierley, watching the road through her kitchen window. When Obed Abernethy dressed in his finest clothes on a busy June afternoon, Agatha investigated and discovered that the Abernethys were adopting an orphan. After Nell Harcourt arrived and proved to be a girl rather than the expected boy, Agatha visited Grey Shutters and insulted Nell's freckles and red hair, causing Nell to fly into a furious rage. Nell later apologized, and Agatha readily forgave her. Over the following years, Agatha maintained her prominent role in Brierley society, organizing events like the Sunday-school picnic ice cream and the Church Aid Society bazaar. Though she originally doubted Nell's upbringing, Agatha came to admire Nell's cleverness and transformation into an attractive young woman. When her husband Thomas fell ill and passed away, Agatha faced financial hardship due to a farm mortgage and medical debts. Thirza Abernethy invited Agatha to live at Grey Shutters in the north gable, allowing Nell to pursue her college education at Wexcombe while Agatha kept Thirza company.

value: Anthony was taken in by Mrs. Laurence Tulk
unit: Anthony was taken in by his aunt, Mrs. Laurence Tulk, and enrolled in Brierley school. He joined the Regent's entrance class under Miss Thorne and eventually passed his Entrance examinations along with his classmates. When Nell Harcourt became the schoolteacher, Anthony initially disdained her and tested her authority, such as by putting a mouse in her desk drawer. After Nell lost her temper and whipped him, Anthony surprisingly developed a deep respect for her, stating her beating was 'just as good as a man's.'

value: In August, Barney drove his double-seated buggy.
unit: In August, Barney drove his double-seated buggy carrying his sister Odette, Nell Harcourt, and Isolde Pembroke to a fundraising concert at the Pale Sands Hotel. He insisted on having Nell sit beside him on the front seat, feeling immense pride in her company despite his inability to converse. During the journey, he mostly smirked and laughed softly without being able to form verbal replies. Upon arriving at the hotel, he hid away and fled out of sheer dread at the prospect of being invited to supper with the performers and guests, though he waited outside with the team to drive the girls safely home after the event concluded.

unit: In August, Barney drove his double-seated buggy carrying his sister Odette, Nell Harcourt, and Isolde Pembroke to a fundraising concert at the Pale Sands Hotel. He insisted on having Nell sit beside him on the front seat, feeling immense pride in her company despite his inability to converse. During the journey, he mostly smirked and laughed softly without being able to form verbal replies. Upon arriving at the hotel, he hid away and fled out of sheer dread at the prospect of being invited to supper with the performers and guests, though he waited outside with the team to drive the girls safely home after the event concluded.

value: Belinda is industrious.

label: History
value: Belinda came to reside at Echo Cottage.
unit: Belinda came to reside at Echo Cottage to serve as maid for Rosalind Penrose, following three of her elder sisters who had previously filled the same role. Because Rosalind continually called her predecessor by the name Belinda, she adopted the designation 'Belinda the Fourth'. She dutifully managed domestic tasks and indulged Rosalind's pretend tea parties and imaginative games. When Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke stumbled upon Echo Cottage, Belinda welcomed them warmly and struck up a close friendship with Nell, whom she tried to imitate. When Stephen Stanhope returned to woo Rosalind, Belinda excitedly followed the romance and cheered for their union. On the day of Rosalind and Stephen's wedding at Echo Cottage, she assisted with preparations and threw a shoe for good luck that struck the minister. Following the wedding, she prepared to accompany the newlyweds to live with them in Boston.

label: History
value: Cedric was born in the United States.
unit: Cedric was born in the United States to Stephen Stanhope and his American wife. Following his mother's death, his father sent ten-year-old Cedric to live with his grandmother on the shore road in Brierley. Upon joining the local school, he instantly formed a special friendship with his new teacher, Nell Harcourt, who appreciated his imaginative nature and sensitive spirit. During his time at school, he excelled as a student, defended younger classmates, and befriended Nell through shared stories and gifts of wild flowers. He also developed a close bond with Miss Rosalind Penrose of Echo Cottage. When his father visited Brierley, Cedric helped re-establish the connection between Stephen and Rosalind, leading to their eventual marriage. Following their wedding, plans were made for Cedric to move to Boston with his father and new mother.

value: Flossie Tulk attended Brierley School.

During Sunday-school and regular classes, she frequently mocked Nell and engaged in dishonest practices like peeking at her textbook during spelling. When Nell was punished by being forced to stand on the dais or sit next to Hugh Carrow, Flossie reacted with spiteful grins. She participated in the Brierley Sunday-school picnic and later joined the class in welcoming the new teacher, Miss Agnes Thorne. When the students formed the Regent's Academy preparatory class under Miss Thorne, Flossie joined despite complaining about the workload and expressing vanity about her family's wealth, claiming she did not need a license to earn a living. During a party at the Pembroke home, Flossie challenged Nell to walk the ridgepole of a kitchen roof; when Nell fell and was injured, Flossie was terrified by thoughts of guilt until Nell recovered. Later, Flossie attended Regent's Academy in Port Marlow along with her classmates, residing in the same boarding house as Frank Stockley. At the Academy, she developed a reputation for having a caustic tongue and continued her petty rivalries, such as falling out with Julia Bell for three months after making rude comments about her. She completed the Second Class coursework and returned to Regent's for a second year.

label: History
value: Honora studied at Regent's Academy.
unit: Honora studied at Regent's Academy, where she became part of a close circle of contemplative and imaginative friends with Nell Harcourt and Mabel Colby. After graduating, she secured a position as the schoolteacher at the Delford school. During her time in Delford, she joined the Brierley Village Improvement Society and contributed by composing an essay for one of its gatherings. In July, her aunt, the famous author Charlotte E. Varley, visited her, and Honora drove her to Brierley to visit Nell at Grey Shutters. The following May, she joined Nell, Isolde Pembroke, and Odette Pullen on a day-long spring picnic through the woods and fields of Brierley, during which they discovered the hidden, abandoned garden of Dinah Wren.

label: History
value: Hugh returned to Brierley school in Fourth Book
unit: Hugh returned to Brierley school in Fourth Book after spending the summer in New Brunswick and three prior years in Alberta. He immediately established a fierce academic rivalry with Nell Harcourt after pulling her braid and calling her 'Carrots', which resulted in her breaking her slate over his head. Though he tried to apologize, Nell refused to forgive him, prompting a years-long rivalry where they competed for top marks. He participated actively in community and school events, reciting 'Bingen on the Rhine' at the Debating Club concert and co-founding the Brierley Village Improvement Society, serving as its president. He rescued Nell from a collapsing pier support on the Lake of Glassy Waters during a game of 'Elaine', but when he asked to be friends, she coldly rejected him, leading him to vow never to ask again. Despite their distance, they both advanced to Fifth Class and then Regent's Academy, where they competed for the Gold Medal and Avery Scholarship. Hugh won the Gold Medal and tied with Nell at the head of the entrance pass list, while Nell won the Avery. To earn money for medical college, Hugh took a teaching post at Pale Sands for a year. Learning that Nell wished to teach locally in Brierley, Hugh voluntarily withdrew his application for the Brierley school so the trustees would hire her instead. Following this selfless act, Nell thanked him and they reconciled, becoming close friends and study partners. Hugh eventually left for Wexcombe College alongside Nell after winning his medal and completing his teaching year.

unit: Hugh returned to Brierley school in Fourth Book after spending the summer in New Brunswick and three prior years in Alberta. He immediately established a fierce academic rivalry with Nell Harcourt after pulling her braid and calling her 'Carrots', which resulted in her breaking her slate over his head. Though he tried to apologize, Nell refused to forgive him, prompting a years-long rivalry where they competed for top marks. He participated actively in community and school events, reciting 'Bingen on the Rhine' at the Debating Club concert and co-founding the Brierley Village Improvement Society, serving as its president. He rescued Nell from a collapsing pier support on the Lake of Glassy Waters during a game of 'Elaine', but when he asked to be friends, she coldly rejected him, leading him to vow never to ask again. Despite their distance, they both advanced to Fifth Class and then Regent's Academy, where they competed for the Gold Medal and Avery Scholarship. Hugh won the Gold Medal and tied with Nell at the head of the entrance pass list, while Nell won the Avery. To earn money for medical college, Hugh took a teaching post at Pale Sands for a year. Learning that Nell wished to teach locally in Brierley, Hugh voluntarily withdrew his application for the Brierley school so the trustees would hire her instead. Following this selfless act, Nell thanked him and they reconciled, becoming close friends and study partners. Hugh eventually left for Wexcombe College alongside Nell after winning his medal and completing his teaching year.

label: History
value: Isolde grows up on her family's farm
unit: Isolde grows up on her family's farm at Pear Hill in Brierley. After Nell Harcourt moves to nearby Grey Shutters, the two girls meet in the Pembroke garden and swear an oath of solemn, lifelong friendship over a path they pretend is flowing water. They establish a playhouse named Larkrise in a nearby birch grove and share games, books, and imaginative names for local landmarks. After Nell accidentally serves Isolde homemade currant wine instead of raspberry cordial, Isolde's mother briefly forbids her from playing with Nell, but the ban is lifted after Nell successfully treats Isolde's younger sister Posy Fay for a severe case of croup. Later, Isolde attends a local concert and sleeps over with Nell at Pear Hill, where their playful jump onto the spare-room bed startles their visiting great-aunt Lavinia; despite initial anger, Aunt Lavinia is charmed by Nell and agrees to fund music lessons for Isolde. As the years pass, Isolde attends Brierley school alongside Nell, participating in the story-writing club, the Brierley Village Improvement Society, and school performances. Though she does not pursue high school entrance exams at Regent's Academy like Nell, Isolde remains her closest confidante and provides steadfast emotional support. Eventually, Isolde becomes engaged to Gideon Duckett, with plans to marry once they reach adulthood.

label: History
value: Mary Farrow fell gravely ill in East Welby.
unit: Lucy's mother, Mary Farrow, fell gravely ill in East Welby and requested that her third cousin, Thirza Abernethy, take in Lucy and her twin brother, Robin. When Mary passed away, Thirza brought Lucy and Robin to live at Grey Shutters. Though Lucy was extremely well-behaved and neat, she suffered from her twin brother's mischievous pranks, such as having her hair pulled or being tricked into standing on a pigpen fence and falling in. During her first winter at Grey Shutters, her uncle in British Columbia passed away, leaving a two-thousand-dollar trust fund for the twins, ensuring their permanent residence at Grey Shutters. In the autumn after turning seven, she began attending Brierley School alongside Robin.

label: History
value: Nell is mistakenly brought to Brierley by Obed Abernethy
unit: Mistakenly brought to Brierley by Obed Abernethy in place of an expected orphan boy, Nell arrives at Grey Shutters and initially despairs upon learning she is unwanted. However, Obed and Thirza Abernethy decide to keep her, and she quickly forms a deep bond with Obed while adjusting to Thirza's strict discipline. Nell forms a passionate friendship with Isolde Pembroke, naming local landmarks such as Linger Lane, the Lake of Glassy Waters, and the Nymph's Well. After a series of dramatic mishaps—including a furious outburst at Mrs. Agatha Sowerby, an accidental hat decoration at church, and an unintentional poisoning of Isolde with homemade currant wine—she overcomes local prejudice and becomes well-loved in Brierley. Nell enters Brierley School, where she engages in an intense academic rivalry with Hugh Carrow, which culminates in her temporarily quitting school after breaking a slate over his head and being forced to sit beside him. Later, she saves Posy Fay Pembroke from croup using her past experience with infants, restoring her severed friendship with Isolde. She subsequently wins the Avery Scholarship at Regent's Academy, but chooses to forfeit her college plans to remain at Grey Shutters and work as Brierley's schoolteacher to support Thirza after Obed's sudden death. Over her two years of teaching, Nell inspires her students, forms a local Improvement Society, helps raise the orphaned Farrow twins, and reconciles with Hugh Carrow, ultimately deciding to pursue her college degree locally at Grey Shutters.

label: History
value: Obed Abernethy resided at Grey Shutters
unit: Obed Abernethy resided at Grey Shutters with his sister Thirza. Seeking farm assistance due to advancing age, heart trouble, and scarce hired labor, he persuaded Thirza to adopt an orphan boy from Nova Scotia. When he drove to Alder River station to collect the child, he was bewildered to find a talkative, red-haired girl named Nell Harcourt instead. Unable to break the news to her immediately, he brought her back to Grey Shutters and quietly insisted on retaining her despite Thirza's initial objections. Over the following years, Obed developed a deep, indulgent affection for Nell, secretly supporting her desires, comforting her during punishments, and purchasing gifts such as sweeties and a stylish new dress for her. When Nell faced a night-time emergency treating a child with croup, Obed drove through the frozen night to bring a physician from Tullyvale. Years later, after experiencing worsening heart spells, Obed received a letter announcing the failure of the Abbey Bank where all their life savings were kept. The sudden shock triggered a fatal heart attack, and he collapsed in the porch doorway of Grey Shutters, dying instantly.

label: History
value: Odette attended school in Brierley.
unit: Odette attended school in Brierley, preparing for the Regent's Academy entrance exam under Mr. Pidgeon and later Miss Thorne. She participated in various community and school events, including performing music at the Sunday-school picnic and acting in dialogues. During her time at school, she joined Nell Harcourt's Story Club and the Brierley Village Improvement Society, where she served on the hall-painting committee. After passing her Entrance exams, she was offered a teaching position at the Stonebridge school, beginning her career there in the autumn.

label: History
value: Opal attended Brierley school.
unit: Opal attended Brierley school, where she shared classes with Nell Harcourt, Isolde Pembroke, and others. She was known among her peers for reporting gossip about the teacher and for her dramatic emotional reactions to classroom mishaps, such as when Hugh Carrow tied her hair to her chair or when firecrackers exploded in the stove. She participated in the Sunday-school picnic, joined the story-writing club, and took part in the school's Christmas concert in the tableau 'Grace, Hope and Charity.' Later, she entered Regent's Academy to prepare for the Entrance examination to become a teacher. After passing her exams, she secured a teaching position in a town further west.

label: History
value: Mr. Pettifer moved to Brierley.
unit: After moving to Brierley, Mr. Pettifer acquired a reputation as an odd and miserly solitary farmer. Upon discovering Nell Harcourt's Jersey cow trespassing in his oat field multiple times, he confronted Nell in a fury, though her sharp retort about his baldness made him retreat. When Nell accidentally sold his cow to a cattle dealer believing it was her own, she visited him to confess and offered a homemade cake as an apology. Pleased with the cake and her honesty, Mr. Pettifer forgave the error and traded for Nell's cow instead, striking up a warm friendship with her. Later, during a severe thunderstorm, his kitchen chimney was struck by lightning, which killed his beloved parrot Nutmeg. Shortly thereafter, his estranged wife Emily tracked him down in Brierley after seeing an item in a newspaper, and the two reconciled and resumed living together.

unit: After moving to Brierley, Mr. Pettifer acquired a reputation as an odd and miserly solitary farmer. Upon discovering Nell Harcourt's Jersey cow trespassing in his oat field multiple times, he confronted Nell in a fury, though her sharp retort about his baldness made him retreat. When Nell accidentally sold his cow to a cattle dealer believing it was her own, she visited him to confess and offered a homemade cake as an apology. Pleased with the cake and her honesty, Mr. Pettifer forgave the error and traded for Nell's cow instead, striking up a warm friendship with her. Later, during a severe thunderstorm, his kitchen chimney was struck by lightning, which killed his beloved parrot Nutmeg. Shortly thereafter, his estranged wife Emily tracked him down in Brierley after seeing an item in a newspaper, and the two reconciled and resumed living together.

label: History
value: Pidgeon served as the schoolmaster at Brierley school.
unit: Pidgeon served as the schoolmaster at Brierley school, where he lodged at the home of Eben Duckett and secured his position due to his uncle being a school trustee. During his tenure, he spent much of his time pursuing Sukey Pullen, courting her at the back bench and writing verse to her. After Hugh Carrow joined the fourth class and teased Nell Harcourt, Pidgeon disciplined Nell by writing a public scolding on the blackboard and making her stand before the class, and on another occasion forced her to sit beside Hugh, leading Nell to boycott school temporarily. Pidgeon also participated in local events, delivering a recitation of Mark Antony's address at the Brierley Debating Club concert. At the end of the school year, Pidgeon delivered an emotional parting speech to the pupils and departed his position, leaving Brierley to be succeeded by Miss Agnes Thorne.

label: History
value: Robin's mother died in East Welby.
unit: Following the death of his invalid mother in East Welby, six-year-old Robin and his twin sister Lucy were taken to Grey Shutters by Thirza Abernethy. His lively and disruptive presence immediately created a contrast with his quiet sister. On his first Sunday, he dropped a caterpillar down a girl's collar during church services, causing a grand commotion. He frequently got into trouble by climbing onto tables, drenching Lucy under the pump, and trapping her in Mr. Pettifer's toolhouse for amusement. After being reprimanded for lying about Lucy's whereabouts, he sincerely promised Nell never to tell another untruth. Robin started attending Brierley school under Nell Harcourt, forming a rivalry and friendship with his classmate Milty Gammon. When Thirza考虑 selling Grey Shutters, the twins were able to remain permanently after their late uncle left a trust fund for their care.

Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke stumbled upon Echo Cottage by accident while taking a wrong path through the woods and quickly befriended Rosalind, charmed by her youthful spirit and imaginative tea parties. Rosalind formed a close bond with Nell and later met Stephen's son, Cedric, whose resemblance to his father deeply moved her. Recognizing the enduring affection between Rosalind and Stephen, Nell facilitated a meeting between them when Stephen returned to visit Brierley. Stephen visited Echo Cottage, where he and Rosalind reconciled after twenty-five years apart. The two were married under the honeysuckle arbor in her garden in late August, surrounded by close friends, and subsequently left to reside in Boston, planning to return to Echo Cottage every summer.

label: History
value: Thirza resides at Grey Shutters
unit: Thirza resides at Grey Shutters in Brierley with her quiet brother, Obed. Expecting an orphan boy to help on the farm, she is shocked when Obed arrives with a red-haired orphan girl, Nell Harcourt. Although she initially intends to send Nell back, compassion leads Thirza to keep her. She takes on the challenge of raising the imaginative child, teaching her housework, manners, and religious duties. When Obed dies suddenly after losing their savings in a bank failure, Thirza is devastated. Facing failing eyesight and threat of blindness, she considers selling Grey Shutters, but Nell gives up her college scholarship to stay home and teach, enabling them to keep the farm. To help with expenses and companionship, Thirza takes in her orphan third-cousins, the twins Robin and Lucy Farrow, as well as her widowed friend Agatha Sowerby. Over the years, Thirza grows deeply attached to Nell, eventually realizing how completely the girl has transformed her life.

Over the years, Thirza grows deeply attached to Nell, eventually realizing how completely the girl has transformed her life.

label: History
value: Miss Agnes Thorne was hired to take over the Brierley school.
unit: Miss Agnes Thorne was hired to take over the Brierley school, becoming the first female teacher ever employed in the village. Her appointment was initially met with skepticism by some locals who disapproved of her innovative methods, such as holding bi-weekly recitation afternoons, conducting field days in the forest to study nature, and leading daily physical culture exercises. Despite these criticisms, she quickly earned the deep love and admiration of her pupils, including Nell Harcourt.

label: History
value: Miss Thorne organized a Christmas concert in November.
unit: In November, Miss Thorne organized a Christmas concert to raise funds for a schoolhouse flag, guiding her students through weeks of enthusiastic rehearsals. Later in the school year, when Nell was terrified of ghost stories she had invented about the nearby spruce wood, Miss Thorne firmly forced her to walk through the grove at dusk to break her belief in her own daydreams. To help her advanced students prepare for the Regent’s entrance exam, she formed a special after-school study class. Although offered a position at a grade school in her home district, Miss Thorne chose to remain at Brierley to guide her students through their final preparation year. When Nell fell behind in geometry and hid a novel inside her desk during history class, Miss Thorne gently confronted her about her academic dishonesty, prompting Nell to promise strict adherence to her studies. She resigned from Brierley school after successfully guiding her students through the Regent's Entrance examinations.
